story_type: abort system steering motor hot fire test
hook: 7,000 pounds of thrust, aimed a different way every second.
narration: Seven thousand pounds of thrust, and this motor picks a new direction every second.
It rides on top of Orion, NASA's moon capsule, as part of the launch abort system.
If the rocket below ever failed, that system would pull the crew away from it.
This motor is the steering. Hot gas burns the whole time, and eight valves choose which port it escapes from. The capsule gets pushed the opposite way.
In this test at Elkton, Maryland, every valve had to open exactly when it was told.
Thirty seconds of switching fire, with nobody touching it but the computer.
outcome: Every valve fired on command, and the team called it a success.
title: 7,000 pounds of thrust that steers Orion
description:
In March 2019 NASA and Northrop Grumman hot fired the attitude control motor of Orion's launch abort system at Elkton, Maryland, to qualify it for spaceflight. Every valve fired on command and the test was a success.
